prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept
Asset type: final in-game environment concept for a Chinese top-down hand-painted 2D prison/factory escape game.
Primary request: redesign ONLY the guard duty room ("值班室") according to the guard room outlined in red in reference image 1, with a practical modular art design that can be built in the existing Godot game. Produce one polished, convincing final gameplay-view concept, not an asset sheet or editor screenshot.
Input images: Image 1 is the PRIMARY approved map layout and material reference: focus on its red-outlined small duty room, north-side equipment, west-side storage, east-side L-shaped wooden registration desk, guard standing in centre-left, single south entrance. Ignore its red annotation and coloured route arrows. Image 2 is the current editor view for existing pale concrete wall caps, muted green-grey flooring, neighbouring office facade and entry orientation; its current empty elongated room is precisely what needs improvement. Image 3 is the existing approved guard sprite style; use ONE small standing guard matching its big head, dark blue-grey work uniform and cap, brown belt and keys, black ink outlines. It is a sprite sheet reference, NOT nine characters.
Composition: a clean near-orthographic bird's-eye gameplay view, screen-aligned horizontal and vertical walls, north at top, no isometric diamond and no tilted floor grid. One whole compact rectangular room, roof removed, all four walls and central south doorway readable, with a narrow strip of surrounding green-grey paved corridor and a little grass behind. Room interior width to depth approximately 380:440; avoid the previous long empty 380:640 hall. Keep a wide 180-unit south opening and front facade aligned with a subtle adjacent office wall fragment on the right. The open-room floor, wall elevation and objects use the SAME fixed projection as the map. Furnishings have restrained top surfaces and vertical fronts, not a different camera angle.
Layout: north-left a tall worn slate-blue metal personal locker; north-centre a LOW communications cabinet/work surface with a simple old desk radio/intercom and two charging walkie-talkies, a small cream round wall clock above; north-right a wall-mounted shallow key cabinet with visible hanging brass keys and a compact paper duty roster board. Along west wall a slender wood and metal file shelf, folders and a few capped supplies; do not fill the floor with random crates. Middle/east an L-shaped honey-brown wooden duty desk with its return against the east wall, a cream open registration ledger and pen, black corded telephone, enamel mug, modest green-shaded task lamp, one wood chair tucked behind the desk. ONE guard stands centre-left, whole body visible, height about 87 relative to 440 room depth. A short bench tucked at southwest wall, one modest old potted plant near the southeast interior corner. A broad continuous central/left passage leads from the south doorway to the duty desk and key cabinet; minimum about 100 world units clear, no stool or object obstructing the doorway.
Materials: retain factory/prison atmosphere, cream aged plaster walls with dark blue-grey protective lower band and slim pale stone coping, simple dusty grey-green small square concrete tiles, weathered warm wood, blue-grey steel, dull brass handles. Wear concentrated on edges, readable large colour shapes, restrained crisp texture and outlines; no sandy noise blanket. Warm neutral daylight with soft contact shadows; clearer and cleaner than the low-resolution original map, still coherent with its painterly art. Duty room is a gatekeeper's registration, key custody and communication room; no medical green ceramic dado, no hospital double sliding door, no blue bed, no monitors wall (that belongs in the adjacent surveillance room), no luxury office, no futuristic tech, no weapons display.
Door: a dark blue-grey manual steel door with a small upper viewing window, opened flat towards the exterior SIDE of its left jamb; frame, slim lintel and threshold separate and clearly visible. Keep the centre passage unobstructed and guard unoccluded. No door open across the walking lane.
Text: one small cream wall plaque above/near the entrance reading EXACTLY "值班室"; optional tiny physical roster heading "值班表". No huge floor title, no UI, no labels/callouts/arrows/route lines, no dimensions, no watermark.
Deliver a complete coherent final effect concept, viewed as if from the game's normal camera, not a photorealistic render or a mood painting.
